correctness.rationale: For a positive prime-two orbit, the distinct prey coordinates satisfy \(0<a<b<1\). An exact factored formula gives \(v_2-v_1>0\), hence the predator multipliers satisfy \(R(a)=k>1>k^{-1}=R(b)\). Their difference forces \(q>[(1+ca)(1+cb)]^{-1}>(1+c)^{-2}\), while positive mortality forces \(q<(1+ca)^{-1}<1\). Conversely choose \(a\) satisfying both strict local bounds, take \(b\) sufficiently close above \(a\), and use the explicit formulas for \(\beta,\theta,r\). Their positive one-sided limits establish existence at every interior ratio. Exact rational witness and 36 constructed rational examples replayed, and symbolic identities were independently checked; the theorem follows from the general analytic proof, not finite enumeration.

value.rationale: A natural full parameter-fiber existence classification, with both sharp universal boundaries and a constructive realization at every interior toxin-to-conversion ratio. It distinguishes toxin-driven nonmonotonic predator response from the linear/saturation-only exclusion and yields testable algebraic boundaries independent of mortality or absolute conversion rate. Stability and global viability are not claimed.
